items.quote: he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering.
items.claim: The text requires a person guilty of these property wrongs to pay back the full value to the owner plus one fifth more. The payment is due on the same day as his trespass offering.
items.actor: the guilty party ("a soul" that has sinned)
items.action: restore the principal and add a fifth part
items.object: property wrongfully taken, withheld, or falsely sworn about
items.mechanism: restitution of the principal plus a 20% surcharge, paid to the owner and tied to the trespass offering

items.quote: lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or in a thing taken away by violence, or hath deceived his neighbour; 6:3 Or have found that which was lost, and lieth concerning it, and sweareth falsely
items.claim: The restitution rule covers several wrongs against a neighbour: lying about goods left in one's keeping, lying about a partnership, taking something by violence, deceiving a neighbour, and lying or swearing falsely about lost property one has found.
items.actor: a soul who sins against a neighbour
items.action: commit a trespass through deceit, violence, or false oath
items.object: a neighbour's deposited, shared, seized, or lost property
items.mechanism: the text counts wrongs against a neighbour's property as a trespass against the LORD

items.quote: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
items.claim: The text presents the rule as spoken by the LORD to Moses. This is the text's own framing, not independent evidence of who wrote it or when. Identifying the passage as Leviticus 6:1-5 (KJV) comes from model-prior and is unverified.
items.actor: the LORD (as the text presents it)
